text:
Juraj Slafkovský has scored once since Oct. 20, and the Canadiens have hardly noticed: they've won eight of their last ten. He has 12 points in 17 games, 10 of them assists, playing 18 minutes a night.

The goals are the outlier. He has two on 5.7 expected goals, a 4.9% shooting rate for a player whose shot speed ranks in the 95th percentile and whose talent range centres on 13.5%. That kind of gap tends to close, because goals follow chances. Our projection still has him around 21 goals.

After the Nov. 5 win over Utah, a night he set up a Nick Suzuki goal, The Athletic's Arpon Basu wrote that "the version of Juraj Slafkovský we saw will need to be the version we see from now on." Two nights later in Toronto, The Hockey News' Karine Hains noted Montreal killed off a Slafkovsky double minor on the way to a 4-2 win. At 22, fresh off eight points in six Olympic games for Slovakia, the next step is simple: finish.
headline: Slafkovsky's goals haven't caught up to him yet
